name: Spain
genZNote: Spain's empire was once so vast that 'the sun never set' on it — and today that legacy lives on in the fact that Spanish is an official language across roughly 20 countries, mostly on a completely different continent.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Occupies most of the Iberian Peninsula in Southwestern Europe, bordered by Portugal, France, and Andorra, with coastlines on the Atlantic and Mediterranean.
Diverse terrain including the central Meseta plateau, the Pyrenees mountains bordering France, and the Canary and Balearic Island groups.
Includes territories in North Africa (Ceuta and Melilla) bordering Morocco, a source of occasional diplomatic sensitivity.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Spanish (Castilian) is the national official language, alongside co-official regional languages including Catalan, Basque, and Galician.
Strong regional identities, particularly in Catalonia and the Basque Country, which have distinct languages, culture, and periodic autonomy/independence movements.
Globally influential culture through flamenco music and dance, bullfighting traditions, and world-renowned art (Picasso, Dalí, Velázquez, Gaudí's architecture).

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A parliamentary constitutional monarchy; the King is head of state while an elected Prime Minister leads the government, under the 1978 democratic Constitution.
Transitioned to democracy after the death of dictator Francisco Franco in 1975, following decades of authoritarian rule.
Composed of 17 autonomous communities with varying degrees of self-governance, including highly autonomous regions like Catalonia and the Basque Country.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A significant contributor to renewable energy technology, particularly solar and wind power engineering.
Home to strong pharmaceutical and biomedical research institutions, alongside a globally respected public healthcare system.
Historic global exploration legacy (backing Columbus's voyages) that reshaped global trade and cultural exchange from the late 15th century onward.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A founding-era member of the European Union (joined 1986) and a NATO member, playing an active role in European policy.
Maintains deep cultural, linguistic, and economic ties across Latin America through its colonial-era Spanish-speaking legacy.
An active participant in Mediterranean and North African regional diplomacy given its geographic proximity to Morocco.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Spain maintain a growing 'Strategic Partnership', with expanding cooperation in renewable energy, infrastructure, defence, and trade.
Spanish companies have invested significantly in Indian renewable energy and infrastructure projects, particularly solar power.
Growing tourism, cultural, and educational exchange between the two countries in recent years.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A major European economy strong in tourism, automotive manufacturing, renewable energy, and agriculture (notably olive oil, wine, and citrus).
One of the world's most visited countries for tourism, with iconic destinations including Barcelona, Madrid, and the Balearic Islands.
A global leader in renewable energy infrastructure, particularly wind and solar power generation.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Flamenco music and dance, and a rich artistic heritage (Picasso, Dalí, Gaudí).
Being one of the world's most visited tourist destinations.
A historic global colonial and exploratory legacy that spread the Spanish language across the Americas.
Strong renewable energy engineering and infrastructure investment.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Euro (EUR).
A major European economy with strengths in tourism (one of the world's most-visited countries), automobiles, and renewable energy.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Diverse landscapes including the Pyrenees, Mediterranean coastline, and semi-arid interior plateaus.
A global leader in solar and wind power generation capacity.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Unified as a kingdom in the late 15th century under Ferdinand and Isabella, the same year Columbus's voyage began Spanish exploration of the Americas.
Built one of history's largest global empires; endured a civil war (1936-1939) followed by the Franco dictatorship until 1975.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1975 death of Franco led to a peaceful transition to democracy.
The 1978 Constitution established a parliamentary constitutional monarchy and devolved significant autonomy to Spain's regions.

sections.heading: 🚀 Space, Innovation & Modern Development
bullets: Instituto Nacional de Técnica Aeroespacial (INTA) supports national space activities within the European Space Agency framework.
Home to significant renewable-energy engineering and infrastructure innovation.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Football is central to national culture, with a FIFA World Cup title (2010) and globally dominant clubs.
Flamenco is recognised by UNESCO as Intangible Cultural Heritage.
Antoni Gaudí's Sagrada Família and other works in Barcelona are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Member of the EU and NATO.
Member of the UN and the G20; maintains close cultural and economic ties with Latin America.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Spain is a Southwestern European parliamentary constitutional monarchy on the Iberian Peninsula, a democracy since 1978 with deep global linguistic and cultural influence via its colonial history.
keyFacts: Parliamentary constitutional monarchy under the 1978 Constitution.
Transitioned to democracy in 1975 after Franco's death ended decades of dictatorship.
17 autonomous communities, including highly autonomous Catalonia and the Basque Country.
commonConfusion: Spain's regional languages (Catalan, Basque, Galician) are co-official in their respective regions alongside Castilian Spanish — they are not dialects of Spanish.

highYieldFacts: Spain: parliamentary constitutional monarchy since 1978; democracy restored after Franco's 1975 death.
17 autonomous communities; Catalonia and Basque Country have strong autonomy movements.
India-Spain: Strategic Partnership; major Spanish investment in Indian renewable energy.
commonTraps: Assuming Spanish is the only official language in Spain — Catalan, Basque, and Galician are co-official regionally.
Confusing Spain's constitutional monarchy with an absolute one — the King's role is largely ceremonial.
mustRemember: Spain: constitutional monarchy since 1978, regionally diverse (Catalonia/Basque autonomy), key India renewable energy investor.
